page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base clock of 2.7 GHz. Compute resources comprise 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading (2 threads per core). Cache allocation includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. The instruction set features AVX, AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory provisioning stands at 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a classic 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for non-volatile persistence. Networking performance provides a baseline bandwidth capacity of 4 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs or hardware accelerators are provisioned on this configuration.

Benchmark analysis shows strong single-core execution, with Geekbench single-core reaching 2000.0 and stress-ng single-core achieving 3074.67 (both placing within the top 25%). Multi-core and throughput metrics primarily sit in the middle 50% tier, indicated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7722.0, a PassMark CPU score of 14487.06, and redis SET performance at 11.15 million operations per second. Large block memory read throughput drops to 38.79 GB/sec (bottom 25%), whereas small block cached read bandwidth achieves 607.06 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration provides balanced resource density suited for standard enterprise workloads. Given its balanced CPU-to-memory allocation and capable single-thread compute capabilities, the instance fits web application serving, CI/CD compilation tasks, enterprise backends, and moderate relational or in-memory caching databases.

Architectural support covers AVX-512 vector and cryptographic instructions. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and providing a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core compute performance alongside mid-tier multi-threaded and memory-write metrics, with redis processing reaching 11.15 million operations per second. The balanced resource configuration is well suited for web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and general caching workloads.
